topics.name: Personal and Social Well-being: Orientation / Baseline
subtopics: Orientation to rules and procedures; baseline assessment in Home Language and Mathematics
Previous year's CAPS skills, knowledge and values covered; showing respect, love and acceptance

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: Orientation / Baseline
subtopics: Orientation to rules and procedures; baseline in Home Language and Mathematics

topics.name: Personal and Social Well-being: About me
subtopics: Timeline of own life: date of birth, starting school, at least one interesting fact; sequencing events and calendar dates
An interesting object from my past: show and tell; research by asking adults and recording

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: About me
subtopics: Understand time and change; represent time chronologically in pictures and words
Timeline of own life (my first tooth, my first step, first day at play school)
The time in your life is part of your history; an interesting object from my past (show and tell)

topics.name: Personal and Social Well-being: Feelings
subtopics: Things that make me happy and sad; recognising feelings such as anger, fear, worry and loneliness
Good ways to express what we feel; apologies: how to say sorry

topics.name: Personal and Social Well-being: Health protection
subtopics: Basic first aid practices in situations such as nose bleeds, animal bites, cuts and burns
Basic health and hygiene, including not touching other people's blood

topics.name: Personal and Social Well-being: Keeping my body safe
subtopics: We are not safe with everyone; rules to keep my body safe; trusting 'yes' and 'no' feelings
How to say 'no' to any form of abuse; how to report abuse (focus on prevention of physical and sexual abuse)

topics.name: Personal and Social Well-being: Rights and responsibility
subtopics: Learners' rights and responsibilities; rights and responsibilities of others at home and at school
Rights and responsibilities of others in our community and in the environment

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: Rights and responsibility
subtopics: Children's rights and how to exercise them: every child has a right to basic nutrition, shelter, health care and social services
The right to be protected from maltreatment, neglect, abuse and degradation

topics.name: Creative Arts: Create in 2D
subtopics: Formal teaching of drawing and painting: exploring a variety of media (week 3)
Introduce overlapping: behind, in front of (week 7)
Variation of paper size and format: working in different scales and degrees of detail (weeks 3, 7)

topics.name: Creative Arts: Create in 3D (box sculptures)
subtopics: Clay modelling: animals, (pet) dragons, pinch pots (week 5)
Art elements: shape/form, texture (weeks 3, 7)
Simple modelling techniques: rolling, pinching, modelling; surface texture treatment (week 5)
Use of tools: safety, consideration of others, sharing resources (week 5)

topics.name: Creative Arts: Visual literacy
subtopics: Art elements: identify and name all art elements (weeks 3, 7)
Use artworks and visual stimuli to relate to own work (weeks 3, 7)

topics.name: Creative Arts (Performing Arts): Creative games and skills
subtopics: Warming up: co-ordination of isolated body parts (arms swinging, swaying) (week 1)
Warming up by focusing on breathing ('painting with your breath', 'panting like a dog') (weeks 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10)
Warming up the voice and singing songs (unison, rounds, call and response) in tune and in time (weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, 10)
Drama games developing interaction and cause and effect (counting games, name games) (week 3)
Playing rhythm patterns and simple polyrhythms in 2, 3 or 4 time on percussion instruments (weeks 3, 5)
Locomotor movement: skip or gallop forwards, backwards, sideways and turning in different pathways (diagonal, circles, S-shapes) (weeks 6, 9)
Non-locomotor movements: bending, rising, reaching, co-ordinating arms and legs in time to music (weeks 6, 9)
Cooling down and relaxation: expressing moods and ideas through movement (weeks 6, 9)

topics.name: Creative Arts (Performing Arts): Improvise and interpret
subtopics: Listen to South African music (indigenous and western) focusing on rhythm and beat in 2, 3 or 4 time (week 1)
Perform notated rhythm patterns (semibreves, minims, crotchets, quavers and rests) using body percussion (weeks 3, 7)
Role play with a beginning, middle and end using a stimulus (South African poem, story, song or picture) (weeks 1, 4, 6, 8)
Portray characters and objects in role play using observation, imitation and exaggeration (weeks 3, 5, 10)
Learn and combine movements from South African dance (e.g. Indian dance, Pantsula) with appropriate music (weeks 2, 4, 6)

topics.name: Physical Education: Laterality
subtopics: Kick a moving ball with the left and right foot (weeks 1, 3)

topics.name: Physical Education: Rhythm
subtopics: Athletics: crouch start in sprinting (on your marks, get set, go) (weeks 4, 7)
Athletics: long jump action, determining the take-off foot (weeks 4, 7)

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge and Personal and Social Well-being: Consolidation of Term 1 themes and coverage
subtopics: Weeks 1-4 are allocated to Term 1 "themes and coverage": use the Term 2 ATP or extend weeks to cover this term's topics linked to Home Language

topics.name: Personal and Social Well-being: Healthy eating
subtopics: Food groups: vitamins (fruit and vegetables), carbohydrates (bread, maize meal), proteins (eggs, beans, meat, nuts), dairy (milk, cheese, yoghurt)
A balanced diet; healthy eating habits; why each food group is good for us
Energy makes us move and work; we need food to give us energy

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: Healthy eating
subtopics: How to make bread; why does bread rise?
How to make cheese; understanding processes (investigate and communicate)

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: Insects
subtopics: Characteristics of an insect: the body, body parts, movement; different insects such as a fly
How insects help us and how some insects harm us

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: Life cycles
subtopics: What a life cycle is; stages of a life cycle; classifying the animal
Life cycle of an amphibian (frog) and of a bird (chicken)

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: Recycling
subtopics: What happens to our waste; re-using, recycling and reducing; what cannot be recycled
Recycling at home and at school; making compost from things that decompose
Technological process: understand reduce, re-use and recycle; classify rubbish that can and cannot be recycled; solutions to reduce littering and becoming active citizens

topics.name: Creative Arts: Create in 2D
subtopics: Formal teaching of drawing and painting: exploring a variety of media (weeks 5, 7, 9)
Greater awareness of the body in motion; overlapping (weeks 5, 7, 9)

topics.name: Creative Arts: Create in 3D (box sculptures)
subtopics: Simple construction techniques to create box sculpture: stacking, joining, surface decoration (weeks 10, 11)
Spatial awareness: extend conscious awareness of working in space (week 6)

topics.name: Creative Arts: Visual literacy
subtopics: Use art elements and design principles in description and discussion; introduce balance (weeks 5, 7)
Use artworks and visual stimuli to relate to own work (week 8)
Describe own artwork using art vocabulary consciously (weeks 5, 7, 10)

topics.name: Creative Arts (Performing Arts): Creative games and skills
subtopics: Warming up: posture and alignment of knees over the middle toes when bending; pointing feet (weeks 5, 6, 9, 10, 11)
Warming up: articulation and vocal tone using rhymes, songs, creative games and tongue twisters (weeks 7, 8)
Rhythm games: listening skills, recalling contrasting rhythm patterns, keeping a steady beat, using different timbres (weeks 7, 8)
Developing control, co-ordination, balance and elevation in jumping actions with soft landings (week 10)
Locomotor and non-locomotor movements with co-ordinated arm movements in time to music (weeks 5, 6, 9, 11)
Cooling down and relaxation: lying on the back, breathing in and out, visualising colour (weeks 5, 6, 9, 11)

topics.name: Creative Arts (Performing Arts): Improvise and interpret
subtopics: Interpret and rehearse South African songs: rounds, call and response (weeks 5, 7, 9, 11)
Movement sentence with a beginning, middle and end on a selected topic, in small groups (weeks 6, 8, 10)

topics.name: Physical Education: Locomotor
subtopics: Simulation activities on the spot: running like a horse, walking like a duck, jumping like a frog (weeks 5, 7)

topics.name: Physical Education: Perceptual motor
subtopics: Catch and throw a ball (paper ball) (weeks 6, 8, 10)

topics.name: Physical Education: Laterality
subtopics: Hand apparatus sequences (short ribbons or scarves) requiring left and right actions (weeks 5, 7)

topics.name: Physical Education: Sports and games
subtopics: Indigenous games: 5 stones played solo on the table (weeks 6, 9, 11)

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge and Personal and Social Well-being: Consolidation of Term 1 themes and coverage
subtopics: Weeks 1-4 are allocated to "themes and coverage": use the Term 2 ATP or extend weeks to cover Term 3 topics linked to Home Language (e.g. 3 weeks Public safety, 2 weeks Pollution, 2 weeks How people lived long ago)

topics.name: Personal and Social Well-being: Public safety
subtopics: Dangerous places to play: rubbish dumps, train tracks, roads, construction sites
Riding trains and taxis safely; dangers of electricity; poisonous and inflammable substances
Signs that warn us of danger; what to do in the face of danger and how to protect ourselves

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: Pollution
subtopics: What pollution is; different types of pollution: water, land, air, noise
Effects of pollution on people and on the environment (cause and effect)

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: How people lived long ago
subtopics: Stories and experiences of older family and community members; objects they used
Old pictures and photographs; how people lived then and now (change and continuity)

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: Space
subtopics: Earth from space: what it looks like (land, sea, clouds); stars and planets and what they are
Names of the planets; telescopes; space travel
What satellites are and the information we get; observing the sky (visit a planetarium or observatory where possible)

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge and Personal and Social Well-being: Consolidation of topics
subtopics: Consolidation of the term's topics

topics.name: Creative Arts: Create in 2D
subtopics: Drawing and painting: exploring a variety of media (weeks 6, 8)
Observation and interpretation of pattern and printmaking in the personal world: overlapping, border patterns, shape within shape, repetition (week 7)
Design principles: conscious application and naming of contrast, proportion, emphasis and balance (week 9)
Pattern and printmaking with found objects and different media for sensory-motor experience (week 5)

topics.name: Creative Arts: Create in 3D (construction)
subtopics: Craft from recyclable materials: patterned frames for own artworks, containers for the classroom (weeks 9, 10)
Art elements: naming and using geometric and organic shapes and forms (week 6)
Emphasis on pattern and surface decoration for craft objects (week 10)

topics.name: Creative Arts: Visual literacy
subtopics: Awareness of pattern and printmaking in Africa (Ndebele painting, beadwork, decorative ceramics): looking, talking, listening (week 8)

topics.name: Creative Arts (Performing Arts): Creative games and skills
subtopics: Warming up the body: combining body parts and isolations (circles with wrists and hips simultaneously) (weeks 6, 8, 10)
Warming up the voice: expressiveness and involvement in poetry, rhymes and creative drama games (weeks 5, 7, 9)
Observation and concentration skills: drama activities such as building a mime sequence in pairs (weeks 6, 8)
Body percussion to accompany South African music, focusing on cyclic (circular) rhythm patterns (weeks 5, 7, 9)
Linking movements in short movement sentences and remembering them (weeks 8, 10)
Swaying combined with spinning movements to soothing music (weeks 5, 7, 9)
Cooling down and relaxation: stretching slowly in different directions to slow, soothing music (weeks 6, 7, 9, 10)

topics.name: Creative Arts (Performing Arts): Improvise and interpret
subtopics: Create a movement sentence in small groups and use it to make patterns (week 7)
Compose cyclic rhythm patterns based on South African music with appropriate tempo and dynamic choices (week 8)
Classroom dramas: different characters through vocal and physical characterisation (the mother, the grandfather, the doctor) (weeks 5, 7, 11)
Poetry performances in groups: choral verse combined with movement and gestures (weeks 6, 8, 10)

topics.name: Physical Education: Locomotor
subtopics: Non-locomotor movements (twisting, turning, bending, curling) combined and co-ordinated in groups (weeks 5, 7, 9)
Jumping while standing (bend knees on landing) (week 6)
Leaping and simulating actions (kangaroo, springbuck, rabbit) (weeks 8, 10)

topics.name: Physical Education: Balance
subtopics: Stand and walk on tiptoe and heel (weeks 5, 7, 10)
Crawling on hands and knees (weeks 6, 8)
Balance walking forward and backward (weeks 7, 10)

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge and Personal and Social Well-being: Consolidation of Term 3 themes and coverage
subtopics: Weeks 1-3 are allocated to "themes and coverage" (Term 3 in the PSW, Creative Arts and PE plans; Term 1 in the BK plan): use the Term 3 ATP or extend weeks to cover Term 4 topics linked to Home Language

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: Products and processes
subtopics: Plants: what we get from plants; process from sugar cane to sugar
The earth: what we get from the earth; process from clay to brick
Matter and materials: materials and preserving; observe, compare, communicate

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: Disasters and what we should do
subtopics: Types of disaster: floods, fire; other phenomena: lightning, earthquakes, storms and strong winds
The effect of disasters on people and the environment; use personal experiences and newspaper and television reports

topics.name: Personal and Social Well-being: Animals and creatures that help us
subtopics: Food we eat and clothes I wear (animals that provide them)

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge: Animals and creatures that help us
subtopics: Animals that give us food and/or clothes: bees, chickens, cows, sheep
Animals that work for us: guide dogs, watch dogs, sniffer dogs, donkeys and horses; stories of other helpful animals (dolphins)

topics.name: Beginning Knowledge and Personal and Social Well-being: Consolidation of topics
subtopics: Consolidation of the term's topics

topics.name: Creative Arts: Create in 2D
subtopics: Drawing and painting: exploring a variety of media (weeks 6, 8)
Drawing overlapping, the body in motion, compositions of more than two people (weeks 6, 8)

topics.name: Creative Arts: Create in 3D (constructing)
subtopics: Craft technique of papier-mâché: create objects by pasting, cutting, tearing, smoothing (weeks 5, 10)
Art elements: texture, shape/form (weeks 7, 8)
Spatial awareness: extend conscious awareness of working in space (weeks 5, 9)

topics.name: Creative Arts: Visual literacy
subtopics: Art elements: identify and name all art elements (weeks 5, 7, 8)
Design principles: name and use contrast, proportion, emphasis and balance (week 6)
Questions to deepen and extend observation of elements and design principles (week 8)

topics.name: Creative Arts (Performing Arts): Creative games and skills
subtopics: Warming up: lengthening and curling the spine (weeks 4, 6, 8, 9)
Creative drama games developing focus and visualisation ('throwing' an imaginary ball: size, shape, weight) (weeks 5, 8)
Responding to stimuli (pictures, phrases, idioms, drama games, poems, rhymes) to explore body language, gestures and facial expression (weeks 4, 5, 7, 8)
Locomotor: control and a strong back (walk with pride, march like a soldier) (weeks 6, 7)
Cooling down and relaxation: tightening all the muscles, then releasing them (weeks 4, 6, 8)

topics.name: Creative Arts (Performing Arts): Improvise and interpret
subtopics: Listening to South African music: how tempo, dynamics and timbre contribute to a unique sound (weeks 6, 7, 8)
Listen to and identify prominent South African instruments and their unique qualities (weeks 5, 7)
Creating a mood with verbal dynamics, expressive sounds and movement, using a poem, picture or song (weeks 4, 6, 8)
Creating movements based on pictures: a movement sentence showing beginning, middle and end (weeks 5, 9)

topics.name: Physical Education: Perceptual motor
subtopics: Shadow imitations: one learner copies the movements of another (weeks 5, 7, 10)

topics.name: Physical Education: Rhythm
subtopics: Rhythmic sequence with or without apparatus (weeks 4, 6, 9)
